label: Darwall argues that favorable outcomes alone do not establish authority to demand their realization
paraphrase: On Darwall's view, showing that an action promotes an objectively better state of affairs, or that a policy would improve reason-compliance, does not by itself establish that someone can demand the action as owed or hold an agent accountable for not acting. Justification of the relevant second-personal authority and the validity of its demand is a further task, which a realist theory may attempt to discharge.
